text: In $\triangle ABC$ shown in the figure, $AB = 7$, $BC = 8$, $CA = 9$, and $\overline{AH}$ is an altitude. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on sides $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AB}$, respectively, so that $\overline{BD}$ and $\overline{CE}$ are angle bisectors, intersecting $\overline{AH}$ at $Q$ and $P$, respectively. What is $PQ$?
figure: Triangle ABC with A at the bottom left, B at the bottom right and C at the top. Side AB is labeled 7, side BC is labeled 8 and side CA is labeled 9. Point H is on side BC, much closer to B than to C, and the altitude AH is drawn (no right-angle mark is shown). Point D is on side AC and segment BD is drawn; point E is on side AB and segment CE is drawn. CE crosses AH at P and BD crosses AH at Q, with P closer to A and Q closer to H.
